To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diets of wheat and Bengal gram decreased the brain glutamate metabolism and that fortification with lysine and methionine + methionine and tryptopphan restored the glutamate metabolism.
the diets containing Bengalgram and wheat as sole sources of protein were found to be inadequate for growth and caused significant changes in the metabolism of glutamic acid and GABA in the brain.
the Bengalgram and wheat proteins, which have low levels of essential amino acids, caused a decrease in the levels of glutamate and its related amino acids in rat brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary protein quality on the brain glutamate metabolism.
the effect of wheat and Bengal gram diets on glutamate metabolism in the rat brain.
the study of the effect of dietary protein on the brain metabolism of glutamate in postweanlings rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diets containing wheat and Bengalgram protein are deficient in essential amino acids and that these deficiencies are responsible for the observed alterations.

the wheat and Bengalgram proteins were inferior in quality as compared to casein protein and that the fortification of wheat and Bengalgran with lysine and methionine, respectively, improved the protein quality.

wheat and Bengalgram are deficient in amino acids essential for the synthesis and maintenance of brain proteins and that the amino acids which were added to wheat and Bengalgram were sufficient to meet the amino acid requirements of brain protein synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wheat and Bengalgram are poor in protein quality and the fortification of these cereals with amino acids improves the protein quality and the nutritional value.
the protein deficiency in wheat and Bengalgram fed rats was associated with decreased levels of brain glutamic acid metabolism.

the decrease in glutamine synthetise, glutamate decarboylase and glutaminase activities in brain of rats fed wheat and Bengalgram may be attributed to the deficiency of lysine, methionine and cystine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fortification of wheat and Bengal gram with essential amino acids can improve the nutritional quality of these diets.
wheat and Bengal gram protein are deficient in essential amino acids, lysine and methionine, which are required for the growth and development of the brain.
the fortification of wheat and Bengal gram diets with amino acid mixture restored the brain RNA, protein, free alpha amino nitrogen and enzyme activities of glutamate metabolism.
